       coalesce((select json_agg(name) from storage.objects where bucket_id = 'document-images' and name like $1 || '/%'), '[]'::json) as old_images;

parameters.content:
# RAG – Ingestion
Keeps the knowledge base in step with the SharePoint library. Every 15 minutes it compares SharePoint with what is already stored, then processes up to 4 new or changed files (small batches keep each run light; a run is skipped while the previous one is still going).

**Documents:** OCR → images → sections → vectors
**Spreadsheets:** rows into a SQL table
**Deleted files:** forgotten everywhere

**Writes to:** Supabase tables `documents`, `document_rows`, `document_metadata`, `ingestion_log` + the image bucket.
**How to watch it:** the `ingestion_log` table and the 8 AM Telegram message. Successful runs are not kept in n8n's Executions list (only failures are).

Time limit: 30 min per run (workflow settings). Rarely an OCR request is lost and the run would wait forever; the limit cancels it and the files are retried. (For a big backlog: run every 2 min — the overlap guard makes that safe.)

## ① Start & safety check
The 15-minute schedule (or the manual button) starts a run.

First it asks n8n's own database whether another ingestion run is still going. If so, this run stops — two runs at once would process the same files (double cost, duplicate passages).

## ② What's in SharePoint right now
Two views of the same folder, joined by file name (the episode's dual-path design):
- **Graph** → each file's permanent ID + content fingerprint
- **SharePoint node** → last-modified time

Names are URL-decoded (%20 → space) so both sides match. `OLD_` and "Do Not Use" files are dropped here, so they count as absent — and are forgotten if they were indexed before.

Reads the top level **and every subfolder** (one level; folders named DNU / "Do Not Use" are skipped). Files in a folder are named `Folder/File.ext`.

nodes.name: ② What is in SharePoint now

parameters.content:
## ③ What changed since last run
Compares SharePoint now with `document_metadata` — the system's memory of what it has processed.
- **new / updated** → processed in the next sections
- **touch** (tags or date changed, same content) → only the date is updated, no re-OCR
- **deleted** → its passages, rows and images are removed: the AI forgets it

Nothing changed → the run ends here.

nodes.name: ③ What changed since last run

parameters.content:
## ④ Pick a batch & download
Takes up to 4 files per run (a backlog clears over several runs). Was 10 — a batch of 8 large PDFs (51 OCR parts) froze a run.

For each file: clear any old passages, rows and images first (so reprocessing never creates duplicates) → download it from Graph by its file ID → route by type: **spreadsheet** · **text** · **document / image** · **unsupported** (logged and skipped, e.g. .mp4, .dgn).

nodes.name: ④ Pick a batch and download

parameters.content:
## ⑤ Spreadsheets → SQL table
Excel rows from **every tab** are stored as they are (one JSON record per row, tab name in `_sheet`) in `document_rows` — not cut up or embedded. The workbook is unzipped only to read its list of tabs.

That lets the agent answer number questions with SQL instead of doing arithmetic itself. Empty sheets are recorded as `empty` so they aren't retried.

**Zip archives** (bottom row): unzipped; rainfall distribution tables (.tbl) inside become rows too — tab = table file name, columns Distribution, Time (hr) and Cumulative fraction.

## ⑥ Prepare documents for OCR
Azure's OCR takes at most 30 pages / 30 MB per request.

**Gotenberg** (a document-conversion container) converts Word and PowerPoint to PDF (images at 150 dpi — smaller and reads better) and splits every PDF into **10-page parts**. Images go through as one part. Upload names are made safe — an apostrophe in a file name once broke conversion.

If Gotenberg can't convert or split a file, the original goes to OCR whole (Mistral reads PDF/DOCX/PPTX up to 30 pages) instead of failing.

## ⑦ Read the pages — Mistral OCR on Azure (US)
Each part goes to Mistral Document AI, paced one every 7 seconds (limit: 10 a minute). It returns the text as markdown plus a **description of every image**.

Parts are checked and joined back into one document in page order. All-or-nothing: a temporary error → **retry** next run; a broken file → **failed** and skipped until someone edits it.

**Photos with no text** (OCR finds nothing) are described by gpt-5.4-mini instead (bottom row), then go through the normal path — so they're still searchable.

## ⑧ Images → Supabase Storage
Skips tiny and repeated images (logos, icons), uploads the rest to the `document-images` bucket, and puts each image's link and description into the text exactly where it appeared.

That's how answers can show screenshots under the right step. Failed uploads are counted and logged.

## ⑨ Cut into sections, embed, store
**GPT-5.4 mini** reads each document as numbered blocks and returns only the cut points (sections of about 500–2,000 tokens); code then cuts the original text, so nothing is reworded.

Each passage is embedded (**text-embedding-3-small**, 1,536 numbers for its meaning) and saved to `documents` with its label: file ID, file name, position. Last: the file is marked processed in `document_metadata`.

(Text files such as .log join here directly — no OCR needed.)

parameters.query:
with ins as (
  insert into document_rows (file_id, file_name, row_data)
  select $1, $2, r from jsonb_array_elements($5::jsonb) r
  returning 1
), log as (
  insert into ingestion_log (file_id, file_name, step, status, chunk_count, message)
  select $1, $2, 'rows_write', case when count(*) = 0 then 'skipped' else 'ok' end, count(*), $6 from ins
)
insert into document_metadata (file_id, file_name, last_modified, content_hash)
values ($1, $2, $3::timestamptz, $4)
on conflict (file_id) do update
  set file_name = excluded.file_name, last_modified = excluded.last_modified,
      content_hash = excluded.content_hash, updated_at = now();
